configuration.discovery: Configuration is discovered from the process working directory, which is this folder - the same as running `kriya generate` here. A kriya.yaml at the root of the repository that contains this folder (this folder itself when it is in no repository), else the Kriya installation, is read; fields only the operator may set need a durable approval.

health.detail: Verification commands run only in an isolating container with the network denied - there is no setting that turns this off; writes are limited to the authorized scope; credential-bearing files are protected paths; secrets are redacted from evidence.
evidence: configuration load: a non-mandatory containment value is refused (ContainmentOptOutError)
health.label: Security

health.detail: Kriya's run state directory is this user's own and closed to others.
evidence: observed: the state directory's owner and mode
health.label: Private state

health.detail: Public lookup is off: nothing leaves this machine for knowledge. Enable it only through the operator configuration.
health.label: Outward lookup

health.detail: A goal that asks for observable behaviour is verified by running the generated application in containment.
health.label: Runtime verification

health.detail: A failed attempt is diagnosed and retried against the exact failure; a run with no progress stops after 2 consecutive attempts.
health.label: Recovery

health.detail: The Java language server (jdtls) imports the project's build on the host and has no contained mode, so Kriya never starts it; code understanding comes from the structural index below.
health.label: Language server

health.detail: Kriya indexes the repository structurally (symbols, references, implementations) and uses it to localize a change; it does not depend on a language server.
health.label: Code intelligence

interaction.note: A change Kriya proposes is held for your review in this window and applied only if you approve it. Any other step that needs a human decision (a knowledge-gap acknowledgement, a skill choice, a command approval) stops the run instead of being approved for you.

toolchains.note: Visibility under this process's own environment (a fixed PATH; no login shell). Which tools a goal needs is only known while the workflow runs; a missing tool then ends the run with Kriya's own typed failure.
